exercises: 빈칸에 알맞은 형태를 쓰세요: 제가 이 근처에 (살다) ____ 우리 집에서 만날까요?

빈칸에 알맞은 형태를 쓰세요: 밖이 (덥다) ____ 안에 있읍시다.
빈칸에 -아서/어서 계열의 명사 형태를 쓰세요: 다들 (휴가) ____ 사무실에 사람이 별로 없어요.

틀린 곳을 찾아 문장 전체를 고쳐 쓰세요: 어제 잠을 못 잤어서 오늘 너무 피곤해요.

forms.form: V/A + 아서 (어간 끝 모음이 ㅏ, ㅗ)
forms.when: Stem's last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ. 가다 → 가서, 작다 → 작아서, 보다 → 봐서
forms.means: because / so (a plain reason or cause)
forms.exampleMeaning: The room is small, so it's a bit uncomfortable.

forms.when: Any other last vowel. 먹다 → 먹어서, 마시다 → 마셔서, 어렵다 → 어려워서
forms.example: 커피를 많이 마셔서 잠이 안 와요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I drank a lot of coffee, so I can't fall asleep.

forms.when: Verbs and adjectives ending in 하다. 피곤하다 → 피곤해서, 공부하다 → 공부해서
forms.exampleMeaning: I was so tired that I went to bed early.

forms.when: Nouns. After a final consonant: 이라서 (학생이라서). After a vowel: 라서 (친구라서). 이어서/여서 is also used.
forms.exampleMeaning: I'm still a student, so I don't have much money.

forms.when: Stem ends in a vowel: 가다 → 가니까. Stem ends in ㄹ: drop the ㄹ, then add 니까 (멀다 → 머니까).
forms.means: because / since. It can come before a command or suggestion.
forms.exampleMeaning: That restaurant is far, so let's take a taxi.

forms.when: Stem ends in a consonant: 먹다 → 먹으니까, 많다 → 많으니까. ㅂ-irregular: ㅂ → 우 + 니까 (어렵다 → 어려우니까).
forms.means: because / since. It can come before a command or suggestion.
forms.exampleMeaning: There are a lot of people right now, so shall we come back another time?

forms.when: Nouns. After a final consonant: 이니까 (회의 중이니까). After a vowel: 니까 (친구니까).
forms.means: since (it) is N. It can come before a command or suggestion.
forms.exampleMeaning: I'm in a meeting right now, so please call later.

objective: Choose between -아서/어서 and -(으)니까 for a reason clause, build the correct form (including nouns and ㄹ/ㅂ irregular stems), and fix sentences that use -아서/어서 before a command/suggestion or with a past-tense marker.
summary: Both -아서/어서 and -(으)니까 give a reason ("because, so"). This sheet shows how to form each one with verbs, adjectives and nouns (including ㄹ- and ㅂ-irregular stems). It also covers the two rules learners break most: only -(으)니까 can come before a command or suggestion (-(으)세요, -(으)ㅂ시다, -(으)ㄹ까요?), and a past-tense marker never goes before -아서/어서 (no -았/었어서).
title: 이유 말하기: -아서/어서와 -(으)니까
watchOut: If the second clause is a command or suggestion (-(으)세요, -(으)ㅂ시다, -(으)ㄹ까요?), use -(으)니까, not -아서/어서. 배가 고파서 밥 먹으러 갑시다 (X) → 배가 고프니까 밥 먹으러 갑시다 (O)
Never put the past marker -았/었- before -아서/어서. The second clause already shows the time. 어제 많이 먹었어서 배가 아파요 (X) → 어제 많이 먹어서 배가 아파요 (O). With -(으)니까, the past is fine: 영화가 벌써 시작했으니까 빨리 들어갑시다 (O)
ㄹ-stem verbs and adjectives drop the ㄹ before 니까, and you do not add 으. 멀으니까 (X) → 머니까 (O), 알으니까 (X) → 아니까 (O). With -아서/어서 the ㄹ stays: 멀어서, 알아서
Most ㅂ-stem adjectives change ㅂ to 우. 어렵으니까 (X) → 어려우니까 (O), 춥어서 (X) → 추워서 (O)
When you thank someone or apologize, use -아서/어서, not -(으)니까. 기다리게 하니까 미안해요 (X) → 기다리게 해서 미안해요 (O)
Nouns: check for a final consonant (받침). 학생라서 (X) → 학생이라서 (O), 의사이라서 (X) → 의사라서 (O). 니까 works the same way: 이니까 after a consonant, 니까 after a vowel.
